analysis.evidence: In מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם, “king of Sodom,” סְדֹם names the city ruled by the king. The parallel phrase וּמֶלֶךְ עֲמֹרָה, “and the king of Gomorrah,” confirms the reading.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וּמֶלֶךְ עֲמֹרָה means “and the king of Gomorrah.” It follows מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם, “the king of Sodom,” in a list of rulers who went out to battle.
analysis.morphology: וּ is the conjunction “and.” מֶלֶךְ is a masculine singular noun in the construct state, governed by the following place name עֲמֹרָה.
